facts.statement: The study used a secondary analysis of data from a longitudinal cohort.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The participants were people of working age who were part of a national database and had records at the time of injury and at 1, 2, 5, and 10 years later.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The main outcome measured was whether the participants were working at 1, 2, 5, and 10 years after their brain injury.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Statistical modeling showed that having a job before the injury was the strongest factor associated with having a job at every follow-up time point.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: People who were working at the time of their injury were more likely to be working at 1, 2, and 5 years after the injury.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Being employed at 1, 2, or 5 years after the injury was associated with a higher chance of being employed at all later time points.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Being married was only associated with a higher chance of employment at the 1-year mark after the injury.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Being able to travel independently was linked to a higher chance of employment, while having more functional limitations was linked to a lower chance of employment at all time points.
facts.subject: humans
